Understanding 3.3.1 asks that the error be indicated in text without mandating where; WAI-ARIA 1.2 lists the checkbox among the roles that take aria-invalid and aria-errormessage; Material gives the checkbox error states but no error text. No token, CSS, template or theme changes now.

decisions.text: The message of a severity sits under the description, for every severity and every control: the description stays visible, and the control's aria-describedby lists the description, then the message. In a group the message sits after the options, as today. The message does not replace the description, the description is not moved above the control, and no line is reserved for the message.
decisions.rationale: Options. A: under the description. B: replaces the description, as the Figma prototype and Material's guideline do. C: replaces it for errors only. D: the description above the control. E: the message line reserved. B removes the shift only when the field has a one-line description and a one-line message; otherwise the field still moves (with no description +24 px, with a two-line message +18 px, with a two-line description it moves up 36 px), the help disappears when people need it to fix an error (a format, a limit), and in a group it moves the options up 29 px, under the pointer. C hides the help for errors only, the one case where people act, and gives a field two heights. D changes the look decided for the Text field family and every screen with descriptions. E makes every field 24 px taller (85 to 109 px) whether it ever shows a message or not; it may come back as a choice of the form's layout in step 10. A keeps the help where it is needed and reads in the order Material's accessibility page gives (supporting text first, followed by the error text); the cost is a shift when a message appears: on a medium Text field (85 px at rest) the next field moves down 24 px for a one-line message and 42 px for a two-line one, and 29 px under a Radio group. No source asks for B on the web: Understanding 3.3.1 mandates no place for an error, and the AccName computation concatenates every referenced node, so a screen reader reads the description, then the message. Material's text field guidelines say to replace the supporting text, so A departs from that guideline, not from Android's accessibility pages. No token, CSS, template or theme changes.

decisions.text: Form controls can show three severities, error, warning and success, set by the severity property (none, error, warning, success; none by default) with one message for every severity. The Text field, the Number field, the Textarea and the Select take all four values; the Checkbox, the Checkbox group and the Radio group take none and error only (our judgment, not a source's). The property and the state invalid and errorMessage are removed, with no alias: the packages are alpha and unreleased, so a clean break (a major change of the specs, 0.x minor). The severity border is the accent functional border, global.border.accent.functional.<severity>.default, and the message color the functional text color, global.text.on-base.functional.<severity>.default. On the web the error is aria-invalid="true" and the severity data-severity; a warning and a success are text and styling only. The accent borders were under 3:1 (the light warning one at 2.13:1 down to 2.01:1, the dark error one, which had no dark value, at 2.82:1 down to 2.11:1), and the team fixed them in the Color foundation 7.1.0 (decision border-accent-functional-3-to-1): warning 500 in light mode, error 400 in dark mode, 3:1 or more on every surface level; the one shortfall left is the light warning border on the subtle warning fill (2.95:1, which step 6 may use as the fill), accepted knowingly by the team (issue #119). Validated, to render in step 6: the severity in the fill, a solid color; the severity icon never inside the typing area, in one place only (after the control, at the start of the message, or nowhere, then the message says the severity); the control keeping its default width without the icon after it.
decisions.rationale: Options. A: errors only, as Apple and Material do (no source for the other two on a field). B: every status (error, warning, success, information), as Fluent does. C: keep invalid and add a separate status property, two properties for one thing. D: errors and success, as the W3C does (a success confirmation with icon and text). The team validated three severities (B without information, which the description covers; W3C confirms a success, only Fluent has a warning). Name: severity was chosen over status (it clashes with the spec's status and with WCAG status messages), intent (it means a destructive action on the Button) and validation; component libraries and developers use severity for success, danger and warning alerts, even if it is odd for success. "Error" over "invalid": the platforms say error (WCAG 3.3.1, Compose error semantics, Material text fields guidelines and accessibility), and invalid is the web's technical term (aria-invalid, :invalid, :user-invalid); Understanding 4.1.3 and the Windows Forms page still use invalid as an adjective of the value. The accent border (rather than the base one) was the team's correction. Sources opened: WCAG Understanding 3.3.1, 3.3.3, 4.1.3, 1.4.1, 1.4.11 and 1.1.1, ARIA21, the WAI notifications tutorial, MDN aria-invalid and :invalid, Apple HIG Writing, Feedback, Text fields and Entering data, Compose semantics, Material text fields guidelines and accessibility, Windows Forms, Text box and LiveSetting.

decisions.text: A form control is a component through which people enter or choose a value the product keeps (text, a number, one or several options, on or off, a point in a range); it has a visible label and may have a description, and when its value can be missing or wrong it can be marked required and report an error. Whether the value applies at once or with the rest of the form depends on how the control is used, not on the component. A button that submits is a form action, not a form control. The components that follow the foundation are the ones whose role profile is marked as input (roles.json), read from each specification: the rules on anatomy and label for every input, on required fields for those with a required property, on validation for those with the invalid state.
decisions.rationale: Labels and instructions are not limited to forms (WCAG 3.3.2), a submit button is activating a control, not changing a setting (WCAG 3.2.2), and Windows tells instantly updating forms from submitting ones, so a control is defined by what people do with it, not by where it sits. The role profiles already name the roles that require WCAG 3.3.2, so the foundation reads them (input) instead of keeping a list. Also considered: a section in each specification declaring when its value applies (at once or on submit), which writes a web submit model into specifications iOS and Android have no source for; a scope per rule, the most precise and the most work; an explicit list of identifiers, which silently leaves a new component out. Known weak spot: the role group is generic, so a future component with the role group that is not an input would be counted as one; revisit it then. Known gap, set aside until the complex controls are aligned after the Text field: the Checkbox has the invalid state and no error message part (the validator warns).

decisions.text: Material's component guidelines (m3.material.io/components/) and Microsoft's Windows app controls guidance and WinUI automation reference are trusted sources, so the form rules for Android and Windows cite those platforms' own guidance.
decisions.rationale: They hold the only Android and Windows guidance on forms (required marking, error text replacing the supporting text, spacing, announcing changes); without them, the foundation could only say these platforms are silent.

changelog.note: Decision forms-choice-error-fill (#105 step 2b, point b3): an unchecked checkbox or radio box in error takes the subtle error fill inside its error border, a checked or indeterminate box keeps its brand fill; the rule severity-fill says so. Checkbox 0.3.0, Checkbox group 0.5.0 and Radio group 0.4.0 gain control.background.error. The error border on the fill 5.45:1 in light mode and 5.14:1 in dark mode (WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1), on the surface levels 0 to 3 unchanged (6.12 / 5.79 / 6.12 / 5.79:1 light, 4.97 / 4.55 / 4.16 / 3.73:1 dark); the fill against the surface 1.12 / 1.06 / 1.12 / 1.06:1 light and 1.03 / 1.12 / 1.23 / 1.37:1 dark, decoration, not the cue. On hover an empty box in error keeps its fill and its error border (before, hover turned its border back to the neutral one).

Decision forms-required-group (#105 step 2b, point b2): a required Checkbox group means at least one option checked, no box carries the required state, the product checks the group and its message says "Choose at least one"; on the web its legend's "(required)" stays in the group's name (aria-required is not supported on group); consents that must all be accepted are separate required Checkboxes; the Radio group is unchanged. The rule required says so; four references (WAI-ARIA aria-required, HTML Checkbox and Radio Button states, HTML-AAM fieldset). The Checkbox group template stops putting required on its first box (Checkbox group 0.4.0).

Decision forms-search-field-severity (#105 step 2b, point b1): the Search field takes the Text field's severities (none, error, warning, success), its message and message part and severityIcon, with the Text field's values. The rule tiers loses its open Search field question; the rule severity-icon names the Search field. One reference (MDN input type search, making input required). No component, token or rendering change here: the field family builds the Search field's severities in #103.

Decision forms-label-column-stacking (#105 step 10, point 8): the rule label-placement says a label column stacks by default when the form itself is narrower than 30 rem (a container query on the web, no script), a product may keep it narrower or move the threshold while meeting 1.4.10 at 320 CSS px, iOS and Android also stack at the largest text sizes. Three guidelines (every platform; web; iOS) and two references (C38, HIG Layout adaptability). Step 10 is decided. No component, token or rendering change here: the field family builds the column.

Decision forms-label-column-gap (#105 step 10, point 7b): a fourth semantic addition owned by Forms, form.gap.label-column → {space.12} (packages/tokens/src/additions/semantic/form.tokens.json), drawn by the Form gaps specimen; the rule label-placement names it for the 12 px between a label column and its controls, the rule spacing counts it among the form's gap tokens. Not an alias of form.gap.title. No rendering change.

Decision forms-label-alignment (#105 step 10, point 7): the rule label-placement says that in a label column every label and legend aligns to the end of a column fitted to the longest label (at most 14 em), 12 px from its control, its first line centred on the box, the description and the message under the control, right-to-left mirrored; stacking left to point 8. One guideline (every platform) and two references (RGAA criterion 11.4, RGAA glossary accolés). No component, token or rendering change here: the field family builds the column.

Decision forms-label-column (#105 step 10, point 6): the rule label-placement says a form sets where its labels sit with labelPlacement (above by default, start), passed to every field-like control as markedFields, one shared column, a group's legend in it, a checkbox, radio or switch label after the box, the setting outside a design tool's variants, Windows' labels always above; alignment and stacking left to points 7 and 8. The Windows guideline says the setting stays above there. No component, token or rendering change here: the field family builds the property.

Decision forms-part-gaps (#105 step 10, point 5, D): the rule spacing says a field's and a group's parts are 6 px apart, a group's description right under its legend (0), options 4 apart (16 in a row), the same on every platform, iOS rows at least 44 pt and Android 48 dp, both 4 apart, macOS as the web, Windows a recorded difference. Three guidelines (every platform; iOS; Android) and two references (HIG Accessibility mobility, Compose minimum target sizes). Select 0.4.0 (gap 4 → 6), Checkbox group 0.3.0 and Radio group 0.3.0 (parts 8 → 6, options 8 → 4, the legend's 0 px fixed). Step 10 points 1 to 5 now decided; the label column (point 6) is next.

Decision forms-gap-tokens (#105 step 10, point 4): three semantic additions owned by the Forms foundation, form.gap.field → {space.16}, form.gap.group → {space.32}, form.gap.title → {space.12} (packages/tokens/src/additions/semantic/form.tokens.json), shown on the Tokens tab by a new specimen (Form gaps); the rule spacing names them, the actions taking the field or the group gap. The screens' form stacks read form.gap.field (16 px, unchanged); the Spacing foundation's rule layout names them (Spacing 0.3.0). Point 5 of step 10 still open.

Decision forms-actions-gap (#105 step 10, point 3): the rule spacing says a form's actions take the gap of what precedes them, space.16 after a form without groups and space.32 after a grouped form, the buttons space.8 apart. Points 4 and 5 of step 10 still open. No component, token or rendering change: the screens' forms already put their actions at the field gap and their buttons 8 px apart.

Decision forms-summary-page-title (#105 step 9, point 6b-2): the rule summary says that on the web a page the server sends back with errors starts its title with the count, "3 errors – " then the page's title, from the product's plural string; after a check in the browser or a live update the title stays; iOS, Android and desktop keep their screen or window title, the focused summary giving the count (the system's judgment). Four guidelines (web; iOS and macOS; Android; Windows) and five references (WAI forms tutorial using the page title, Understanding 2.4.2 intent, Apple HIG Toolbars titles, Android Compose semantics window-like components, Windows Title bar). Step 9 point 6 is complete. No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-group-gap (#105 step 10, point 2): the rule spacing says two groups of fields are space.32 (32 px) apart and a group's title space.12 (12 px) above its first field, a Checkbox or Radio group keeping the field gap, the grouping carried in the code too; Windows' 48 px is a recorded difference. One guideline (every platform) and one reference (HIG Layout, visual hierarchy); the Windows guideline names both differences. Points 3 to 5 of step 10 still open. No component, token or rendering change: no screen groups its fields under titles.

Decision forms-field-gap (#105 step 10, point 1): the rule spacing says two fields are space.16 (16 px) apart at every field size, from a field's last part to the next label, a Checkbox group or a Radio group being one field; Windows' 24 px is a recorded difference. Two guidelines (every platform; Windows) and two references (Windows Forms spacing, WAI forms tutorial visual position of label text). Points 2 to 5 of step 10 still open. No component, token or rendering change: the screens already stack their fields 16 px apart.

Decision forms-summary-server-focus (#105 step 9, point 6b-1): the rules summary and announcement say that on the web a page the server sends back with errors focuses the summary's title, or the only field in error, with the autofocus attribute and no script, with no fragment in that page's URL; iOS, Android and desktop move focus with the decided means once the server answers. Two guidelines (web; iOS, Android and desktop) and two references (HTML autofocus attribute, MDN autofocus). The error count in the page's title is still open (step 9 point 6b-2). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-summary-updates (#105 step 9, point 6a): the rule summary says that the error summary shows the errors of the last submit, fixing a field does not change it, and each submit rebuilds it and focuses its title (one error left: it goes, focus to that field; none: the form is sent); a product whose every check runs in the browser or the app may update it live (an entry leaves, the title's count follows, announced politely), never when a check waits for the server; iOS and macOS (Apple's dynamic validation) and Android (validation as people type) may follow it live, Windows keeps the default, each the system's judgment. Four guidelines (one generic, iOS and macOS, Android, Windows) and three references (WAI forms tutorial overall feedback, Understanding 4.1.3 modification of status text, Android Developers' quick guide Validate input as the user types, its page added to the trusted Android prefixes). The web's page sent back by the server is still open (step 9 point 6b). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-summary-place (#105 step 9, point 5): the rule summary says that the error summary sits at the top of the form, before its first field (in a dialog or a panel, at the top of that form), its title a heading one level below the form's; on iOS, Android and desktop, the first element of the form's scrolling content, not pinned. One guideline and one reference (Understanding 1.3.2). Its updates are still open (step 9 point 6). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-summary-entries (#105 step 9, point 4): the rule summary says that the error summary lists the errors only, one entry per field in the form's order, and that on the web each entry is a plain in-page link to the field's control (a group's first option), no script, the control's scroll-margin-top keeping its label in view; the URL fragment, history and single-page app trade-offs; iOS, Android and desktop move focus as after a submit. One guideline and three references (HTML scrolling to a fragment, HTML navigate to a fragment, MDN scroll-margin-top). Its place and updates are still open (step 9 points 5 and 6). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-summary-title (#105 step 9, point 3): the rule summary says that the error summary's title states the count, "There are 3 errors in this form" (the WAI tutorial's example), the English default the Error summary component holds, the product passing its own translated, pluralised string (one plural string per language); the title states, the entries say the fix. The rule announcement's example follows. One guideline and one reference (MDN Intl.PluralRules). Its entries, place and updates are still open (step 9 points 4 to 6). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-summary-component (#105 step 9, point 2): the rule summary says that a dedicated Error summary component renders the summary, not the Alert (no alert role, its title takes focus, entries are links), built in its own pull request after this foundation (#129); its title and count, entries, place and updates are still open (step 9 points 3 to 6). One guideline and one reference (APG Alert pattern). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-summary-optional (#105 step 9, point 1): the rule summary says that an error summary is optional, shown by default after a failed submit from two fields in error, never with one (focus goes to that field), and that a product may decide never to show one, as a sign-in; when shown, the decided rules on focus, entries and announcements apply; what renders it, its wording, entries, place and updates are still open (step 9 points 2 to 6). One guideline (generic) and two references (WAI tutorial listing errors, Understanding 3.3.1 intent). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-platform-gaps (#105 step 8, point 4): the rule announcement states once that each platform follows its own guidance where it has some and the generic behaviour where it has none, through the API its guideline names as the system's judgment, and that a product may still depart from the default for its own specifics; its "Not decided yet" sentence is removed. Six Apple, Android and Windows guidelines end with the same sentence (the Android announcement guideline gains it); Apple's low-priority caveat is kept. No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-focus-after-submit (#105 step 8, point 3): the rule announcement says that after a failed submit focus moves to the error summary's title when the form has one, otherwise to the first field in error, with each platform's means; five guidelines (generic, web, Apple, Android, Windows); ten references (SCR32, Understanding 3.3.1 native validation, HTML interactive validation, Understanding 4.1.3 excepted examples, MDN tabindex, Apple LayoutChanged and UIKit layoutChanged, SwiftUI AccessibilityFocusState, Compose FocusRequester, Windows programmatic focus). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-warning-success-announcement (#105 step 8, point 2): the rule announcement says that a warning shown on leaving a field and a success from a check people cannot make, when it runs, are announced politely like an error, as "Label: message", through the form's region or announcement on every platform, and that an error clearing as people type is silent; the web, Apple, Android and Windows guidelines name warnings and successes; three guidelines (generic, web, Apple feedback); three references (ARIA22, WAI-ARIA status and aria-relevant). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-error-announcement (#105 step 8, point 1): the rule announcement says that an error appearing as people leave a field is announced politely by the form as the label, a colon and the message, the error summary entry's string, with each platform's means (a polite live region per form on the web, a low-priority announcement on iOS and macOS, a polite live region on Android, LiveSetting Polite on Windows); five guidelines; nine references (ARIA19, Understanding 4.1.3 techniques, WAI-ARIA aria-live and alert, MDN live regions, HIG VoiceOver, Apple Announcement, AppKit announcementRequested, AutomationLiveSetting). No component, token or rendering change.

Decision forms-message-relies-on-label (#105 step 11, point 4; step 11 complete): the rule message-wording says a message relies on its label and does not repeat the field's name, and words an error summary entry as the label, a colon and the message, as a link, the label alone when the message is empty; the rule summary notes it; two guidelines (the summary entry, Android's alert announcement); two references (G139, G83). The examples drop the field's name from their messages. No token or rendering change.

Decision forms-submit-enabled (#105 step 7, point 3; step 7 complete): the rule timing keeps the submit button enabled while required fields are empty (generic rule, web, Android) and lets iOS, macOS and Windows disable it until they are filled, as their guidance says; the rule keyboard says Enter does not submit while it is disabled; three guidelines (web and Android, Apple, Windows) and one reference (APG focusability of disabled controls). The Button 0.30.2 notes the exception. No token or rendering change.

Decision forms-message-punctuation (#105 step 11, point 3): the rule message-wording says a message or a description of one sentence takes no period, two or more sentences each take theirs and a question keeps its mark, in sentence case, a second sentence only when the fix needs it, about one line and two at most; a new guideline; the run-on reading under aria-describedby is recorded. Every example drops the period of its single sentence. Material's grammar and punctuation and Apple's Alerts become references. No token or rendering change.

Decision forms-warning-success-timing (#105 step 7, point 2): the rule timing says a warning follows the error's timing and never blocks the submit, and a success shows only for a check people cannot make themselves, when it runs; the rule statuses points to it; two guidelines (every platform, Apple). The Forms examples already fit (a likely typo, an available username). No token or rendering change.

Decision forms-severity-word-guideline (#103 step 22b) supersedes forms-severity-word: with severityIcon none the message's own words say the severity, a guideline the component cannot enforce; the component writes no severity word, and a project that cannot write its own messages (a backend it cannot change) starts them with the severity's word and its language's colon itself. Rules severity-icon and message-wording reworded; the docs' "The icon" and "Writing messages" follow. No token or rendering change.

Fix: the rule severity-icon says that after a multi-line control (the Textarea) the icon sits on the control's first line, as the Textarea draws it, rather than centred on the whole box; the docs say so too and give the shift a message causes under a medium Text field with its 16 px message: 30 px for one line, 54 px for two (was 24 and 42 px, measured before the message took the label's size). No rule or token change.

Decision forms-severity-word (#105 step 11, point 2): the rules severity-icon and message-wording say that with severityIcon none the component writes the severity's word (the icon's translated name and the language's colon) and that the author never types it; the warning and success examples drop their typed word.

Decision forms-validation-timing (#105 step 7, point 1): the rule timing gives the default, recommended timing (an error shows when people leave a field they changed and on submit, never mid-typing, and clears as soon as the value is right), with five guidelines (every platform, web, Apple, Android, Windows); a use case that cannot follow it chooses another timing.

Decision forms-message-says-the-fix (#105 step 11, point 1): a new rule message-wording and a guideline: a message says the fix for every severity, an empty required field reads like any other error, a warning says what to check and a success what was confirmed.

Decision forms-search-alone (#103 step 19, point 3): the rule keyboard and its web guideline exempt a search field that stands alone (the only field of its search form) from the submit button: Enter runs the search.

Decision forms-keyboard (#103 step 19, point 2b): the rule keyboard (focus in reading order, a submit button that Enter submits, the return key's label per platform: the form's action on the web, next on the way on iOS and Android) and its web, iOS, Android and desktop guidelines. Android Developers' Compose focus, keyboard and text guides and Windows' input guidance become trusted sources (a11y/sources.json).

Decision forms-required-windows-name: on Windows the asterisk stays in the accessible name (the UI Automation Name is the label as shown), with IsRequiredForForm. Windows' accessibility guidance and the UI Automation property identifiers become trusted sources (a11y/sources.json).

Decision forms-asterisk-style: on Android and Windows the required asterisk is the error text color (the error message's and the error icon's), the label's size and weight, 4 px after the label (2 px in small), the note's asterisk the same red; 5.79 to 6.12:1 light, 5.30 to 7.06:1 dark. The contrast pair error-text-on-surfaces covers it.

Decision forms-mark-style: the required mark is at the label's size, regular, in the description's color (global.text.on-base.neutral.secondary), the disabled text color when disabled; 12.09 to 12.78:1 light, 6.65 to 9.28:1 dark on levels 0 to 3 and sunken.

Decision forms-marked-fields: which fields a form marks is set once per form, markedFields (optional by default, required, none) on every control that can be marked required; each control draws its mark from its own required. The Text field family carries it from #103 step 16; the Checkbox, the groups and the Select with step 2b.

Decision forms-warning-border-600: the light warning border is warning 600 (Color foundation, border-accent-warning-600): 6.16:1 at the lowest on the surface levels, 5.86:1 on the warning fill (was 2.95:1). The warning and success rendering is complete: warning-border-on-fill, warning- and success-border-on-surfaces and success-text-on-surfaces become required pairs.

Decision forms-warning-one-color: the warning icon and message read one color, warning 600 #765818 in light mode (Color foundation, warning-on-base-600): the message 6.16:1 at the lowest (was 12.36:1), now a required pair; the icon 6.16:1 (was 3.09:1).

Decision forms-severity-icon-glyphs: the warning icon draws warning and the success icon check_circle, the Alert's intent icons; two new required pairs, warning-icon-on-surfaces and success-icon-on-surfaces (3:1).

Decision forms-severity-fill (supersedes forms-error-fill): warning and success are filled like the error, with the subtle functional background of their severity, at rest and on hover alike. Six new pairs on the warning and success fills; the light warning border on its fill is measured only (2.95:1, issue #119).
Decision forms-message-color: the message keeps the functional text color of its severity (a keep decision); the error rendering is complete.
Decision forms-severity-icon-color: the severity icon reads the on-base icon role of its severity (error: global.icon.on-base.functional.error.default), the message text's color, in both placements.

Decision forms-severity-icon-size: the severity icon after the control takes the Button's icon size at the same size (20 / 24 / 24 px), space.8 away; in the message it is 16 px, space.4 before the text. Text only: the icon part comes to the components with its color.

Decision forms-severity-icon-placement: the severity icon after the control, in the message or nowhere, one rule per form through severityIcon (after-control, message, none; message by default); choice controls offer message and none. Text only: the property, the icon part and its tokens come to the components with the icon size and color (step 6).

Decision forms-error-fill: a control in error is filled with the subtle error background, at rest and on hover. The rule on the fill names the token; the error border and text pairs become requirements, with three new pairs on the fill.
Decision forms-required-voiceover: macOS hides "(required)" behind accessibilityRequired, iOS keeps it in the accessibility label. The rule on required fields and an Apple guideline say so.
Apple's UIKit, AppKit and SwiftUI references become trusted sources for Apple platform rules (forms-apple-api-sources).

Decision forms-required-marking-platforms: Android and Windows mark required fields with their own asterisk, explained once (Windows also sets IsRequiredForForm); iOS and macOS apply the generic words. The rule on required fields and three platform guidelines say so; how "(required)" reaches VoiceOver stays open.

Decision forms-required-mark-exposure: on the web, "(required)" is hidden from assistive technology (the required attribute says it once) and "(optional)" is part of the accessible name. The rule on required fields and a web guideline say so.

Decision forms-required-marking: a form marks the fewer fields in words, "(optional)" on optional fields with a note at the top by default, "(required)" on required fields when most fields are optional; no asterisk. The rule on required fields and a web guideline say so.

Decision forms-label-placement: where the label sits is a layout choice; the generic rule (above by default, a label column as a form layout, after the box of a checkbox, a radio or a switch, no floating label) applies as is on the web, and the other platforms follow their own requirements, a floating label allowed where it is the platform's standard (Material on Android). New rule label-placement and platform guidelines.

Decision forms-message-part-every-control: every form control that can show a severity has a message part after its description; the Checkbox gets its message part in step 2b. The rule on the anatomy of a field says so.

Decision forms-message-under-description: the message of a severity sits under the description for every severity, the description stays visible and aria-describedby lists the description, then the message; a group puts the message after its options. The rule on the anatomy of a field says so.

Breaking, decision forms-validation-severities: the invalid status is replaced by three severities, error, warning and success (the severity property, one message for all); the rule on statuses becomes the rule on severities, with the web mapping and the validated rules on the fill, the icon and the width (rendered in step 6); the tiers read the severity property; the measured status borders read the accent functional border. The examples use severity and message, with a warning and a success of the Text field.

A form control is defined by what people do with it, and the foundation applies to every component whose role profile is marked as input; a button that submits is a form action (forms-input-components).
Material's component guidelines and Microsoft's Windows app controls guidance become trusted sources for the form rules on Android and Windows (forms-platform-sources).
